blogs.title: Why Tokens Are Out, and Patches Are In: The Rise of Byte‑Level Language Models
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the problems with traditional tokenizers—bias, multilingual inequity, and fragility to noise—and how the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) replaces them with dynamic byte patches. The post explains the intuition behind letting the model decide patch boundaries based on prediction entropy and why this matters for everyday users of LLMs.

blogs.title: Dynamic Patching Explained: From Fixed‑Size Strides to Entropy‑Driven Byte Groups
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the three patching strategies explored in the BLT paper (static stride, whitespace, and entropy‑based). Readers will learn how each method works, when it’s best suited, and why entropy‑based patching provides a data‑driven way to allocate compute where it’s needed most.

blogs.title: Scaling Language Models Without Tokens: How BLT Matches Llama 3 With Fewer FLOPs
blogs.description: Breaks down the scaling experiments that show BLT achieving parity with token‑based LLMs up to 8 B parameters while using up to 50 % fewer inference FLOPs. Includes easy‑to‑understand graphics and analogies that illustrate the trade‑off between patch size, model size, and compute budget.

blogs.title: Robustness By Design: Byte‑Level Models vs. Tokenizers on Noisy and Low‑Resource Text
blogs.description: Summarizes the robustness tests (noisy inputs, phoneme mapping, CUTE benchmark, low‑resource translation) where BLT outperforms tokenized models. Highlights why direct byte access gives better character‑level understanding and more reliable performance on messy real‑world data.

blogs.title: From Tokenizer to Byte Latent Transformer: Turning Llama 3 Into a Tokenizer‑Free Model
blogs.description: Walks through the “byte‑ify” approach—initializing BLT’s global transformer with a pretrained Llama 3 checkpoint and fine‑tuning only the local encoder/decoder. Shows how this can dramatically cut training FLOPs while preserving performance, offering a practical recipe for developers.

blogs.title: Future Directions for Patch‑Based LLMs: End‑to‑End Patching, Scaling Laws, and Beyond
blogs.description: Explores open research questions raised by the BLT work, such as learning patch boundaries jointly with the model, deriving new scaling laws for byte-level architectures, and optimizing hardware implementations. Provides a forward‑looking perspective for researchers and engineers interested in the next generation of efficient LLMs.
